pageCache.pageTitle: A WARM WELCOMEWHERE TRADITION MEETS EXCELLENCE | Kerem School
pageCache.text:
A WARM WELCOMEWHERE TRADITION MEETS EXCELLENCE
At Kerem Prep, we believe that every child deserves an education that inspires both the mind and the heart. Our small classes and outstanding teachers ensure each pupil is stretched and supported, achieving academic success while discovering a deep sense of belonging within a vibrant Jewish community.
Our exceptional results are achieved through our enriched academic curriculum and innovative, character-building programmes such as ‘How to Be a Mensch’ and our ‘Kerem Challenge Book’. Through these initiatives, we invite pupils to understand that who they are matters as much as what they know, helping them grow into confident, compassionate, successful young people.
We warmly invite you to visit us and experience the ‘Kerem Effect’ for yourselves!
Ms A Rose and Mrs A Sharman
RESULTS AND DESTINATION SCHOOLS
OUTSTANDING RESULTS EXCEPTIONAL FUTURES
At Kerem School, pupils consistently achieve results well above national expectations, reflecting the dedication of our staff, the strength of our curriculum and the personalised support each child receives. Year after year, our graduates secure places at top independent and selective secondary schools – both Jewish and secular – where they continue to thrive as confident and capable learners and leaders.
FACILITIES
A LOOK INSIDE
OUR LOCATIONS
TWO SITES ONE COMMUNITY
18 Kingsley Way, Hampstead Garden Suburb, London N2 0ER
Kerem Early Years Unit provides a caring, stimulating start for children from 9 months, with superb pastoral care and a smooth transition into school life.
Our EYFS-based curriculum supports early literacy, numeracy, creativity, and physical development through play and hands-on learning — all within a warm Jewish environment.
Children grow in confidence, communication, and independence while enjoying tefillah, Ivrit, Torah stories, and celebrations of Shabbat and Chagim.
Norrice Lea, Hampstead Garden Suburb, London, N2 0RE
Kerem Main School offers a nurturing and challenging environment where children thrive academically, socially, and spiritually from Reception through to Year 6.
Our broad, engaging curriculum builds strong foundations in literacy, numeracy, science, humanities, and the arts, while developing critical thinking, creativity, and a love of learning.
Jewish values are at the heart of school life, with daily tefillah, Ivrit, Torah learning, and joyful celebration of Shabbat and Chagim fostering a strong Jewish identity and connection to Israel.
ACADEMIC
HIGHLY ACADEMIC PERSONALISED LEARNING
At Kerem School, we combine high academic standards with a personalised approach to learning, ensuring each child is challenged, supported, and inspired to reach their full potential.
Our dedicated staff nurture individual strengths, tailoring education to meet every learner’s needs in a calm, focused environment. This commitment empowers children to excel beyond expectations and grow into confident, independent thinkers.
SCHOOL LIFE
JEWISH LIFE & LEARNING
At Kerem, our vision is simple yet profound: to spark curiosity, deepen connection, and foster a lifelong love of Jewish learning. From singing and storytelling in the early years to mastering Hebrew reading, Judaism is brought to life every day with joyful, heart-warming experiences and academic rigour, enabling pupils to study Chumash in depth, explore Rashi, and progress to more advanced Jewish texts. Whether through Festivals or daily Tefilah, Kerem children experience Judaism as something to treasure throughout their lives.

pageCache.pageTitle: ISI Inspection | Private School London | Kerem School
pageCache.text:
It is with immense pride that we are publishing the outcome of the recent ISI (Independent Schools Inspectorate) inspection, which took place over 3 days in March 2024.
ISI is similar to Ofsted, in that it reports to the Department for Education on the extent to which schools meet statutory requirements. It upholds rigorous standards for Independent Schools. ISI provides objective, reliable reports on the quality of schools and makes the information available publicly to parents, government, and the wider community. In this way, it helps schools, their staff and governors/proprietors to recognise and build on their strengths and to identify and remedy any deficiencies.
The inspectors report as to whether the school has ‘met’ or ‘not met’ the required statutory standards. In all 5 areas that are required to be inspected, Kerem MET all of the standards. This is a wonderful recognition of our fabulous school and its community, recognising the work that has been done since the last inspection in December 2019.
The early years setting is an immersive and engaging environment which promotes all areas of learning. Adult child ratios are generous and contribute to individual needs being supported, and children making good progress towards the early learning goals.
The early years setting is a vocabulary-rich environment and data shows that the children are consistently ahead of age related expectations in this area, literacy and numeracy skills are promoted well.
In the most effective lessons, teachers plan with the aptitudes and prior learning of pupils in mind. Additional adults are utilised to provide specific support and management of time and behaviour are effective. In these circumstances, pupils are able to acquire new knowledge or skills. Pupils are particularly engaged and self motivated whenever their intellectual or creative interests are promoted.
Pupils benefit from a broad and balanced curriculum.
A recent focus on academic attainment has led to steady improvement in standardised scoring, which illustrates that pupils are making good progress in their literacy and numeracy skills.
In addition, leaders have established tracking systems to measure pupils’ progress within both age groups and subjects. These measures have had a positive impact on individual pupils’ outcomes.
The school community’s connection with its own faith underpins a deep sense of spiritualism in the pupils. Leaders ensure pupils develop tolerance and empathy via a study of world religions from nursery onwards.
As a result of the education about Jewish and other faiths, pupils are respectful towards different backgrounds cultures and religions.
Extra curricular provision is well attended and highly regarded by the pupils. The activities provided enable pupils to hone their skills in areas of interest to them.
Roles within the school pupil committees are highly sought after an application and democratic process elevate the importance of these positions.
The three pupil committees oversee the school’s charitable, environmental and community initiatives responsibly by setting up this structure leaders have given pupil committees a clear purpose if pupils are proud of the contribution they make to the school and wider society.
Leaders prioritise people’s emotional well being by ensuring there are carefully developed programmes of physical personal and health education. appropriate to their needs.
The newly created wellbeing room gives pupils space to reflect on their emotions and strategies to manage them.
Pupils feel safe at school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Values and Ethos | Independent School | Kerem School
pageCache.text:
Our Vision
Kerem’s vision and values are shaped by the conviction that aspiration, effort and belief can transform dreams into reality — reflecting Theodor Herzl’s enduring message, “If you will it, it is no dream” – אִם תִּרְצוּ אֵין זוֹ אַגָּדָה.
We are a Modern Orthodox Jewish school committed to academic excellence, personal growth and a deep, joyful connection to Judaism. We educate confident, thoughtful children who develop a genuine love of Torah and mitzvot, a strong sense of Jewish identity, and the knowledge, skills and character to thrive in the modern world. Jewish and British values are woven through every aspect of school life. We nurture a meaningful connection to Israel and its people, while preparing pupils to play an active and positive role in British society — now and in the future.
If you will it, it is no dream.
Our Values in Action
At Kerem, learning is ambitious, nurturing and joyful. We believe that children achieve their best when academic rigour is combined with warmth, care and a deep understanding of who they are and who they can become.
The Kerem Challenge Book
Each child at Kerem has their own Kerem Challenge Book – Little Acts, Big Impact – which invites them to engage with small but meaningful challenges that encourage kindness, independence, responsibility, and curiosity. The Challenges encompass each of the 3 interconnected principles which shape our approach to personal development.
Myself and My Values
My Faith and My Community

Holistic development
We are committed to educating the whole child. Alongside strong academic outcomes, we place great value on emotional literacy, wellbeing, character and self-belief. Children are encouraged to see themselves as capable, reflective learners with limitless potential. This is supported through:
The 10 Kerem Characteristics
The ‘How to be a Mensch’ programme

Jewish life and learning
Jewish life at Kerem is lived, meaningful and deeply embedded in our daily practice. Through Jewish Studies, Ivrit and our enriched curricular and co-curricular programme, pupils develop a strong connection to Hashem, their community and Israel. Our vibrant approach nurtures children who are:
confident and proud of their Jewish identity,
knowledgeable and engaged in Jewish learning,

We hold high aspirations for every child, regardless of starting point. Our curriculum is carefully designed to build knowledge, skills and understanding over time, while remaining responsive to the needs of each child. Kerem pupils benefit from:

A Shared Commitment to our Vision and Values

Rooted in values and focused on the future, Kerem pupils leave us ready to contribute positively to Jewish life, British society and the wider world.

pageCache.pageTitle: Bursaries | Jewish School London | Kerem School
pageCache.text:
As a charitable foundation, we are committed to making a Kerem education accessible to the widest possible range of children from our community. They have a positive impact, not only on each recipient, but by enriching and diversifying our school community. Each year, we offer several fee-assisted places (bursaries) to eligible families. Bursaries can transform a child’s experience of learning and greatly increase the opportunities available to them in adulthood.​
How our bursaries work
How to apply for a bursary
Please contact admissions@keremschool.co.uk to request an initial bursary enquiry form.
Who can apply for a Bursary?
Bursaries are available to pupils applying to join the School at Reception and in Years 1-6.
Do you qualify for a bursary?
Our financial support is means-tested, so we will need to assess your circumstances before making a decision. Every family is different, so we consider each application individually rather than setting strict thresholds and criteria. We will take into account your sources and amount of income, your outgoings, the size of your family, the number of dependent children and your assets and liabilities. Our funds are limited, so we are not always able to offer as many bursaries as we would wish.
The level of bursary award
Bursary awards range in value according to financial need and the funds available for bursaries. As a rough guide, families with one child whose total household gross income is approximately £150,000 or more will not be eligible for bursary support.
What do bursaries cover?
Bursaries cover the cost of our school fees. Costs such as coach travel, lunches, and educational school trips are not covered.
Annual reassessment
Every year, each bursary is subject to a means-test reassessment. The size of the award for the coming year will only be adjusted up or down if there has been a significant change to the family’s financial circumstances. If your circumstances have changed very significantly and you would not qualify if applying now, your bursary may be withdrawn. Families of bursary award holders are responsible for any remaining school fees not covered by the bursary award.
Who will know?
Bursaries are awarded in confidence. However, many bursary students are happy to tell others and some act as ambassadors, encouraging others to apply or donate financially to the scheme.
Further help with bursaries
If you have any questions, please get in touch. We are very keen that the right students and families benefit from our bursary programme. Please email admissions@keremschool.co.uk or telephone 0208 455 0909.

pageCache.pageTitle: Two Sites, One Community | Kerem School
pageCache.text:
Our Pre-Prep (Nursery and Reception) on the corner of Kingsley Way and Middleway, is a calm and protected setting created especially for our youngest pupils.
Surrounded by high hedges and its own gardens and outdoor learning areas on 3 sides, the Pre-Prep and Little Grapes Nursery provides a secure, familiar space where children quickly feel at home. Learning flows naturally between indoors and outdoors, with daily free-flow play, exploration and hands-on experiences providing a varied, stimulating and exciting learning environment for all our pupils.
As children move into Prep (Years 1–6), they transition to our main school building — a dedicated wing of Hampstead Garden Suburb Synagogue — where they benefit from facilities designed to support growing independence, curiosity and ambition.
Pupils enjoy specialist learning spaces including a STEAM lab, library and wellbeing room, as well as access to the synagogue’s main hall for full-school assemblies, performances, plays and productions. These shared spaces help pupils develop confidence, creativity and a strong sense of community.
As well as its own secure playground, the Prep site also backs directly onto Lyttelton Playing Fields, giving older pupils immediate access to excellent outdoor and sporting facilities, including playing fields, tennis courts and netball courts. Outdoor learning and physical activity remain a valued and regular part of school life as children grow.
Together, our two sites offer the best of both worlds — a warm, secure start for our youngest children, and superb facilities and opportunities for pupils to grow into as they develop into confident, capable and well-rounded learners.

pageCache.pageTitle: Jewish Life And Learning | Private School London | Kerem School
pageCache.text:
Jewish life at Kerem is warm, joyful and deeply embedded in the everyday experience of our pupils. As a Modern Orthodox school, we are committed to traditional Torah values while nurturing confident children who feel secure in their Jewish identity and proud of who they are.
We see parents as valued partners in their child’s Jewish journey. Inspired by the words of the Shema — “You shall teach them to your children and speak of them” — we believe that Jewish education is strongest when school and home work together. Through shared celebrations, communication and community involvement, we aim to support families in nurturing Jewish life beyond the classroom.
Our aim is simple and enduring: to inspire a lifelong love of Judaism, grounded in knowledge, enriched by experience, and lived with joy.
Tefilah
Each day at Kerem begins with Tefilah, creating a calm and reflective start to the morning. Age-appropriate and meaningful, Tefilah helps children develop familiarity with prayer, language and melody, while also encouraging gratitude, mindfulness and a sense of community.
Festivals
The Jewish calendar is celebrated with energy and enthusiasm at Kerem. Festivals are woven naturally into both lessons and wider school life. Jewish Studies and Ivrit are taught by specialist teachers and brought to life through music, art, storytelling, practical activities and shared celebration, helping children understand not only what we do, but why we do it.
Mitzvot
Learning about mitzvot, customs and values in this way fosters a strong sense of pride, ownership and enjoyment in Jewish life, creating lasting memories and a confident connection to Jewish tradition.
Parasha and Chumash
Weekly learning is enriched through the Parasha, which is explored in ways that are thoughtful, accessible and relevant to children’s lives. Stories, discussion, drama and creative activities help pupils connect Torah learning with values such as kindness, responsibility, courage and respect. As children progress through the school, they develop increasing fluency and confidence in Chumash, gaining both knowledge and enjoyment as they encounter texts in greater depth.
Our Connection with Hampstead Garden Suburb Synagogue
Situated within the synagogue premises, Kerem benefits from a uniquely immersive Jewish environment and close links with the local community. This setting reinforces a sense of belonging and continuity, helping pupils understand that Judaism is not confined to lessons, but is a vibrant, living part of everyday life.
Ivrit
At Kerem, Ivrit is taught throughout the school, starting in the early years. Our Ivrit curriculum focuses first and foremost on developing a love of the language and of Israel. Its aim is to teach conversational Ivrit by using the language in everyday situations, so that it can be used confidently beyond the classroom. Whether it is Israeli Breakfast Club, visits from the Israeli Theatre Company or producing their own Fashion Show in Ivrit, pupils have numerous opportunities to engage deeply with Israeli language and culture. You can read more about our Ivrit curriculum here:

Welcome to Little Grapes!
Little Grapes is our nursery provision for children aged 9 months to 3 years. From the age of 3, children join our pre-school nursery which is led by a qualified teacher and teaching assistant team. Children who are in Kerem Nursery have priority status for a place in Kerem Reception.
Little Grapes and Kerem Pre-School Nursery are housed within our beautiful Early Years setting in Kingsley Way, together with our Reception class. Surrounded on three sides by gardens and playgrounds, it is light-filled, secure and carefully designed for young minds to explore the world and develop a joyful love of learning and Judaism.
We believe Little Grapes Nursery offers something truly special: a warm, nurturing environment within a thriving primary school, benefitting from our experienced leadership, specialist teaching input, strong pastoral oversight and deep connection to Jewish values. From the earliest stage, each child will become part of the Kerem community – known, supported and gently prepared for the next steps of their journey.
For more information about Little Grapes, Kerem Pre-School Nursery and our hours and fees, please download our prospectus here.
To teach is to touch a life forever
I am delighted to be joining Little Grapes as Nursery Manager and to be leading this exciting new chapter for our Early Years centre.
I trained as an early-years teacher in South Africa and began my career in Jewish preschools before spending almost sixteen years running the preschool at a leading girls’ school in Cape Town. My career has since taken me around the world, including Taiwan, where I became Director of Tiger Tots and helped it grow into a thriving preschool community of more than 200 children.
More recently, I led Alyth Nursery in London and helped establish Apples and Honey Nightingale, an innovative intergenerational nursery. These experiences have given me a deep understanding of the UK Early Years Foundation Stage, safeguarding and regulatory requirements, as well as the richness of Jewish nursery life.
Throughout my career, my greatest priority has always been the happiness and wellbeing of every child. I believe that young children flourish when they feel safe, understood and cherished, and I look forward to creating a warm, nurturing and connected community for all our Little Grapes children and their families.
I cannot wait to meet your children and become a small part of their story in the very near future.
Hours and Fees
Little Grapes is open 49 weeks per year from 7.30am (early drop off/breakfast) to 6.30pm. We are closed over Peseach and between 24th December and New Year’s Day.
We offer both term-time and year-round nursery packages. Some families prefer care that aligns with the school day and calendar, but early drop-off, longer days and year-round provision is also available.

Before and After School Clubs
From sport and creative arts to languages, problem-solving and performance, our clubs are designed to broaden horizons, encourage independence and nurture curiosity. Whether children are discovering a new passion or deepening an existing one, our co-curricular programme helps them grow in confidence, resilience and teamwork — while enjoying a rich and balanced school life. “Innings and Outings” Trips and In-School Enrichment
We are always looking for meaningful ways to enrich and enhance pupils’ learning. Through our extensive programme of trips and residentials, Kerem pupils gain in knowledge, independence, and confidence and make memories that stay with them long after they leave Kerem. As well as ‘outings’ we also organise ‘innings’ – exciting educational experiences from visiting subject specialists, musicians, dancers and theatre groups, hosted at Kerem.
We aim to ensure that each year group has at least one ‘outing’ and one ‘inning’ per term closely linked to what they are learning in school. From ‘Greek’ Days to drama workshops and from the JW3 Panto to a whole school trip to Kew Gardens to celebrate Tu B’Shevat, these experiences enable pupils to immerse themselves in their studies in exciting and practical ways and bring classroom learning to life.
Some examples of recent enrichment experiences include visiting the Toy Museum in Bethnal Green to support Year 1’s learning about the Great Fire of London and a trip to Southend-on-Sea for Year 2 to develop their understanding of coastal features. By Year 3, learning becomes even more immersive, with pupils stepping back in time at Celtic Harmony to experience life in the Stone Age and Iron Age and visiting Hampton Court Palace to deepen their understanding of the Tudors and Henry VIII, as well as exploring the Living Rainforest to enrich their science and geography studies.
In years 4 – 6 pupils go on residential trips, starting with a one night Shabbaton in year 4, a two night outward bound adventure in Year 5 and a 3 night ‘road trip’ examining the history of the Jewish community in the UK with time spent connecting with other Jewish school communities.

pageCache.pageTitle: Head's Welcome | Prep School | Kerem School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Kerem!
Every day we feel both humbled and privileged to lead this extraordinary community. Our vision is simple but powerful: every child should leave Kerem not only well-educated, but also kind, confident, and ready to make their mark on the world.
We believe that education is about far more than academic achievement; it is about nurturing the whole child to flourish — intellectually, socially, spiritually, and emotionally. Jewish values and traditions are interwoven with a forward-looking, ambitious curriculum which balances academic excellence with strong character development.
Our school motto is Im Tirtzu, ein zo agadah — if you will it, it is no dream – and we work tirelessly, as a whole community, to realise that vision!
Ultimately, what makes Kerem truly special is its people: our children, our dedicated staff, and our supportive families. Together, we create a vibrant, close-knit community where Jewish life is lived joyfully, and where every child is encouraged to dream, to achieve, and to become the very best version of themselves.
We warmly invite you to visit us and see for yourself the difference a Kerem education can make.
Mrs A. Sharman and Ms A. Rose
What makes Kerem an exceptional place to learn?
Small Classes, Skilled Teaching
With average class sizes of 18–22, every child at Kerem is known, supported and challenged. Teachers have the time to understand how each child learns best, encouraging their aspirations and creating a calm, focused and respectful environment where pupils feel confident to contribute, take risks and achieve their full potential.
Personalised Learning, Exceptional Outcomes
Learning at Kerem is carefully tailored to each child, enabling pupils to perform well above national benchmarks from Nursery through to Year 6. Our children achieve outstanding 11+ results, securing places and scholarships at leading north London secondary schools including Haberdashers’, Immanuel, JFS, Highgate, Channing, UCS, City and South Hampstead.
Strong Characters, Shared Values
Education at Kerem is not just about results. We place equal importance on developing character and responsibility. Through our 10 Kerem Characteristics and our unique ‘How to Be a Mensch’ programme, pupils develop the values, language and confidence to act with integrity, compassion and respect. Alongside this, our Kerem Challenge Book encourages children to complete meaningful, age-appropriate challenges, building independence, empathy and resilience from Nursery to Year 6.
Curiosity & Creativity
Our rich and varied curriculum nurtures curiosity and a love of learning. Through our STEAM lab, pupils explore science, technology, engineering, art, coding and robotics, alongside a re-energised English and Maths curriculum, outstanding Jewish Studies provision and Forest School. Our extensive programme of trips, clubs and help pupils discover their passions, develop leadership skills and build lasting friendships.
Superb Pastoral Care and SEND Support
Our superb SEND provision ensures that every child receives the right support in a structured and caring environment. We are equally proud of our pastoral care which supports personal growth while encouraging pupils to look outwards through acts of kindness and charity, to develop a strong sense of responsibility to both Jewish and wider communities.
Our school operates across two sites: Nursery and Reception classes are housed in a building with an exciting outdoor area, while the rest of the school is located on a separate site.
At Kerem, we hold the highest expectations for all our children, both academically—our pupils consistently achieve well above national expectations—and socially. We foster caring attitudes, mutual respect, self-confidence, and leadership skills, helping children to grow into creative, independent thinkers. Our Kerem Characteristics—collaboration, curiosity, flexibility of mind, humour, initiative, middot, persistence, reflectiveness, resilience, and risk-taking—are at the heart of everything we do.
Learning at Kerem is highly personalised, driven by our dedicated staff who ensure every child’s needs are met and their aspirations encouraged.. Our enriched curriculum, which includes Forest School lessons, prepares pupils for life as responsible Jewish citizens by promoting British values and fostering a global outlook. We make learning engaging and fun, providing opportunities for children to exceed their potential.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Story | Prep School London | Kerem School
pageCache.text:
Kerem School was founded in 1948 through the vision and determination of Stanley Frankfurt z”l, who believed passionately that a strong Jewish education was essential for the future of the community. With his encouragement and perseverance, the Hampstead Garden Suburb Jewish Kindergarten opened in the old synagogue hall, laying the foundations for what would become Kerem School.
From the very beginning, the school was guided by values as well as ambition. Dayan Meyer Lew, the first Honorary Principal, suggested the name Kerem — meaning vineyard — expressing the hope that children would grow and flourish as grapes on the vine.
The school quickly became oversubscribed, leading to the acquisition of a purpose-built site in Kingsley Way in 1950, now home to our Nursery and Reception. As the community grew, so did the school, and in 1955 Kerem School for Years 1-6 opened alongside Hampstead Garden Suburb Synagogue.
Over the decades, Kerem has been shaped by the extraordinary commitment of its families, governors and leaders. A significant moment in the school’s history came with the establishment of the David Carson Memorial Fund, which enabled the full refurbishment of the classrooms and the creation of a much-loved playground — a lasting testament to community generosity and shared values.
Kerem has been led by a succession of dedicated headteachers and supported by an active, parent-led governing body, ensuring that the school continues to evolve while remaining true to its founding principles. Milestone anniversaries — including the 60th and 70th celebrations — have recognised Kerem’s contribution to Jewish life locally and beyond, with tributes from community leaders reflecting the school’s enduring impact.
Today, Kerem educates children from Nursery through to Year 6 across two sites, offering a broad and ambitious secular curriculum alongside outstanding Jewish Studies. Thousands of pupils have passed through Kerem’s doors — many returning years later as parents, and even grandparents — a powerful reflection of the school’s legacy.
Rooted in tradition and focused firmly on the future, Kerem continues to nurture confident, thoughtful and values-driven young people, ready to take their place in the world with pride in their Jewish identity. We warmly invite you to visit Kerem and experience our community, our learning and our values for yourself.
